original_test_intent: Stress AMD GPU HBM sequentially with AGFHC exerciser and bandwidth workloads while monitoring GPU/power telemetry, and prove tool success, no memory miscompare, zero relevant RAS delta, no new error evidence and acceptable bandwidth.
original_method: Capture GPU/HBM topology, driver/firmware/tool identities, baseline RAS and timestamped kernel/health state; approve compatible hbm_lvl1/hbm_bw, bandwidth/error semantics and dedicated no-load window; start independent amd-smi and AGT PM logging with verified outputs, run hbm_lvl1 to terminal completion then hbm_bw without overlap, monitor safety continuously and compare complete results, RAS delta, miscompare and time-windowed errors before post-health verification.
manual_activity: The owner approves tools, topology, bandwidth/RAS/error rules and maintenance; an operator starts both monitors and runs the workloads sequentially while watching safety; the owner reviews all acceptance axes and decides the verdict.
required_inputs: Compatible AGFHC hbm_lvl1 and hbm_bw recipes
Compatible amd-smi monitor and AGT builds plus index map
RAS counters/events and allowed zero-delta definition
Relevant dmesg/journal error policy and timestamp boundary
Dedicated maintenance, thermal/power aborts, storage and recovery
safety_requirements: Require explicit approval for heavy HBM stress and no competing GPU load
Run hbm_lvl1 and hbm_bw sequentially, never overlapped
Start/verify amd-smi and AGT logging before stress with unique output paths
Preserve baseline and time-windowed logs instead of clearing them
Monitor GPU, HBM, RAS, thermal, power and system health continuously
Stop on miscompare, RAS increase, new hardware error, GPU loss, limit or monitor failure
Do not rerun after unexplained failure without engineering disposition
agent_execution_scope: Collect topology/tool identities, RAS/log baselines and criteria
Validate two recipes and both independent monitor streams
After approval run sequential workloads once with monitoring
Parse success, miscompare, bandwidth, RAS delta and new-error evidence
Perform no criteria invention, concurrent/uncontrolled stress, recovery or DUT verdict
engineer_actions: Approve recipes/tools, mapping, bandwidth/RAS/error semantics and maintenance controls
Authorize/monitor HBM stress and recovery thresholds
Disposition any failure/miscompare/error/counter/bandwidth issue and issue PASS, FAIL or BLOCKED

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The source demands no dmesg content while asking to clear logs, leaves bandwidth criteria and RAS semantics unspecified, and hard-codes AGT indices without a topology map. DeepSeek uses invalid PARTIAL/insecure access and omits the mandatory monitor, AGT, RAS and full miscompare/error acceptance.

review_improvement: Restores every omitted monitor and acceptance dimension and aligns them in one traceable, non-destructive stress timeline.
independent_technical_reasoning: HBM integrity, bandwidth and system health are distinct outcomes: success return code does not prove data integrity or performance, and a zero absolute RAS value is not meaningful without reset/history semantics. Timestamped baseline-to-post deltas preserve pre-existing evidence while isolating the test window. The source explicitly requires separate monitoring terminals, so monitor failure or wrong GPU indices invalidate observability even if AGFHC completes.
